matches.quote: A second feature or an increased MDC width along Γ′–M′ could arise from: ... surface or surface-resonance states and surface-versus-bulk components
Only 7 K and 200 K are compared... measure a series through T_N... show that the splitting tracks the magnetic order parameter
At 200 K, Fermi–Dirac broadening... can wash out a 0.09 Å⁻¹ double-peak structure... Surface aging, adsorption... during cycling, and reversibility on re-cooling are not addressed.
If DFT is correct, the fitted second peak cannot be the altermagnetic spin partner... the claimed agreement with DFT breaks down precisely where it matters.
A cleaved surface with a Co-covered, Co-depleted or partially covered top layer... The authors should characterize the cleaved surface (core-level spectroscopy, LEED, STM)
measure a series through T_N... extract splitting and linewidth versus T from Fermi–Dirac-divided EDCs/MDCs; show that the splitting tracks the magnetic order parameter
The measurements are entirely spin-integrated... All spin assignments rest on DFT overlays... clearly distinguish calculated from measured spin character in figures and text.

notes: C10 is judged 'partly' because P14 explicitly identifies the issue of Co-covered vs. Co-depleted cleaved surface terminations and asks for surface characterization, but focuses on uncompensated surface magnetism rather than checking whether the dog-bone bands appear on both terminations. C4 is 'partly' because P18 and P14 list surface states as a candidate origin for the splitting near M' without tracing the specific dispersive feature noted by the referee.
